title: Morning Digest, Saturday 28 November 2026
intro: The Centre Party's council meets tomorrow with its leader's job reportedly on the line, a drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian technicians, eurozone leaders pick Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to run the ECB, and OpenAI countersues Apple.

items.title: Drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian defence technicians
items.body: Two Rheinmetall Italia employees maintaining an air-defence radar site died on Thursday and a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani worker were injured. Kuwait and Italy blame Iran; Tehran denies it and calls the attack a false flag, while indirect US-Iran talks remain stalled.

items.title: Eurozone leaders pick Hernández de Cos to lead the ECB
items.body: European Council President António Costa said on Thursday that eurozone states recommend the head of the Bank for International Settlements and former Bank of Spain governor to succeed Christine Lagarde in February; he would be the first Spaniard in the post. Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier were recommended for the executive board. After the European Parliament and the ECB give their opinions, leaders are expected to make the formal appointment at the December summit.
items.source: European Council, 26 Nov; Al Jazeera (AFP, Reuters), 26 Nov

items.title: Centre Party council decides tomorrow, and Thand Ringqvist may go if it says no
items.body: The 59-member förtroenderåd is expected to vote on Sunday on the leadership's plan to let Kristersson through in Monday's 13:00 vote and join an M-C-KD-L minority government. SVT's sources say Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist will resign if the council says no; she has majorities in the party board and Riksdag group behind her. Birgitta Ohlsson says she will vote against Kristersson regardless, and council member Aida Karimli will vote no; S, V and MP say their doors remain open if the council overrules her. If Kristersson loses, a fourth vote is due before Christmas, and a fourth failure means a snap election.
items.source: SVT, TV4, SVT Text, 26-27 Nov (resignation based on unnamed sources)

items.title: Vattenfall raises grid fees by 5 percent
items.body: About 900,000 households and businesses pay more from next year, which the company attributes to grid investment; Ellevio and Eon have not announced 2027 fees.

items.title: Iraq extradites two suspects wanted in Sweden
items.body: A 20-year-old suspected of recruiting for the Foxtrot network and a 21-year-old linked to a 2024 murder in Skärholmen are being sent back, which prosecutors credit to closer cooperation with Baghdad.

items.title: Scheduled
bullets: Sunday 29 November: Centre Party council decides on the Kristersson government; snap general election in Spain.
Monday 30 November: Riksdag votes on Kristersson as prime minister at 13:00; appeal verdict in Sarkozy's Libyan campaign-financing case; AWS re:Invent opens in Las Vegas.
Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats choose between Schumer and Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires; Estonia closes its land border with Russia.
Thursday 3 December: Jensen Huang testifies to the US Senate Banking Committee.

items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple
items.body: OpenAI filed its own suit on Friday, escalating the trade-secrets fight that Apple started in July when it accused former employees of taking confidential hardware information to OpenAI.
items.source: CNN, 27 Nov; Apple's original suit: Al Jazeera, 10 Jul

items.title: Research pulse
bullets: Harness design for robot agents (Google with Emory, Ohio State and others): 470,000 simulated rollouts across eight benchmarks show that even frontier models fail when asked to output gripper poses directly, and work best when they hand motion to a trained action model through sub-goals and write checked control code; the combined recipe lifts frozen action models by up to 43 points without retraining (arXiv 2611.34778, alphaXiv).

Drawing doesn't help models think yet (Princeton, Meta): having a vision-language model request a generated helper image before answering lowered accuracy in 106 of 130 pipeline-task pairs, by 3.7 points on average and 21 on small-object search, mostly because the model asked for the wrong picture (arXiv 2611.34935, alphaXiv).

OS-Omni (OS-Copilot team): a 300-task benchmark of long computer-use workflows across six operating systems finds the best agent, Claude Opus 5.5, at 68.5 percent against 77.3 for humans, with frontier models beating people on Linux but trailing by over 25 points on iOS and macOS (arXiv 2611.34232, second on Hugging Face daily papers).
items.source: arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 24-25 Nov
